risk_if_not_implemented: Without Tainting, the organization's understanding of the threat environment may become stale, leaving defenses misaligned with active adversary tactics. Based on the risk and threat mapping for this control, this deficiency most likely exposes the organization to Loss of Accountability / Attribution (R-AC-1), Undetected / Delayed Detection of Adverse Activity (R-SA-1), and most likely increases susceptibility to Human Error (MT-9).

compensating_control_1.name: Non-Repudiation
compensating_control_1.description: Mechanisms exist to utilize a non-repudiation capability to protect against an individual falsely denying having performed a particular action.
compensating_control_1.justification: Non-Repudiation (MON-34) provides overlapping security capability that compensates for the absence of Tainting (THR-14) by addressing related risk objectives through an alternative control mechanism aligned with Process applicability. Given the process-oriented nature of this control, this compensating control targets the same underlying risk objective through an alternative approach, helping to maintain an acceptable level of residual risk until the primary control can be implemented.

compensating_control_2.name: Session Audit
compensating_control_2.description:
Mechanisms exist to provide session audit capabilities that can: 
(1) Capture and log all content related to a user session; and
(2) Remotely view all content related to an established user session in real time.
compensating_control_2.justification: Session Audit (MON-18.1) provides detective monitoring capability that compensates for the absence of Tainting (THR-14) by identifying unauthorized, anomalous, or non-compliant activity that the primary control would have prevented. Given the process-oriented nature of this control, this compensating control targets the same underlying risk objective through an alternative approach, helping to maintain an acceptable level of residual risk until the primary control can be implemented.
